memory_update.text: SLM is the cleanest direct US-listed private education-loan originator for the student-financing-and-affordability node.
SOFI is the most visible US-listed refinancing platform candidate; exposure is direct but mixed with broader consumer-finance and fintech drivers.
NNI is a key public servicing/systems infrastructure name, with large government-owned and private education-loan servicing volumes.
MMS should be tracked as a federal student-loan servicing contractor via Aidvantage, but student-loan exposure is only one part of a broader government-services business.
NAVI is a below-$1B exception: highly relevant as a legacy private/FFELP education-loan asset owner, but more of a runoff/credit-risk barometer than a growth platform.

Affordability analytics and financial-aid software remain under-covered by public pure plays; likely mappings include diversified software/data vendors such as Workday, TransUnion, Equifax, and private vendors like College Board PowerFAIDS or SightLine, but these were excluded from the top 5 because direct node exposure is weaker or not US-listed pure play.

Primary public-market federal-servicing candidates for this node are Nelnet (NNI) and Maximus (MMS/Aidvantage); MOHELA and EdFinancial appear important but are not straightforward US-listed common-equity candidates.

Private student-credit and refinance candidates include Sallie Mae (SLM), SoFi (SOFI), and Navient (NAVI/Earnest); these are direct but credit-cycle-sensitive rather than pure picks-and-shovels infrastructure suppliers.

The strongest chokepoint signal is not physical scarcity but regulated process capacity: few servicers, complex repayment-plan rules, borrower communications, delinquency/default processing, and compliance obligations.

Affordability analytics and education-verification/data infrastructure remain under-covered in the five-name limit; potential next-pass candidates include Equifax/The Work Number and private companies such as National Student Clearinghouse-linked vendors, Enterval, MARKETview, Sparrow, Tasseled, and PayForED.
Need current market-cap verification for NAVI before treating it as above the USD 1B preferred threshold; retain as direct-exposure candidate but label market-cap note as unknown until checked.
SLM, SOFI, NNI, MMS, and FLYW are the highest-priority US-listed candidates for the student_financing_and_affordability node in this pass.
The node splits into three public-market sub-buckets: private student credit/refinancing, federal loan servicing/BPO infrastructure, and tuition-payment or affordability workflow software.

Potential additional but weaker/less direct mappings to check in later passes: Fiserv as legacy servicing-platform infrastructure, credit bureaus such as Experian/Equifax/TransUnion for underwriting and borrower analytics, employer-benefit platforms for student-loan repayment assistance, and Navient/Earnest for private education finance after federal-servicing exit.

Need a dedicated policy evidence pass on federal borrowing caps, IDR/SAVE replacement rules, PSLF servicing changes, delinquency normalization after repayment restart, and private-loan spread/credit performance.

summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded direct US-listed universe for the student-financing and affordability chokepoint. The strongest direct public-market mappings are private student-loan originators, student-loan refinancing platforms, federal/private loan servicers, and legacy owners of FFELP/private education-loan assets. The node remains policy-mediated: federal portfolio size, delinquency normalization after repayment restart, GradPLUS/Parent PLUS rule changes, servicing contract changes, and borrower credit stress can redirect demand toward private lenders, refinancing platforms, lower-cost programs, or employer/ROI-oriented education models. This is research support only, not a buy/sell recommendation. Expanded universe around the student-financing chokepoint found a small set of US-listed companies with direct exposure to regulated student-loan servicing, private education lending, refinancing, and repayment infrastructure. The clearest scarce-supplier angle is federal loan servicing: Department of Education materials list only a small group of current servicers, with public-market exposure mainly through Nelnet and Maximus/Aidvantage. Private student-credit exposure maps to Sallie Mae, SoFi, and Navient/Earnest, but their economics depend on credit quality, funding costs, regulation, refinancing demand, and borrower stress rather than simply education enrollment growth.
